claims.claim_text: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.
claims.evidence_span: GPTZero's Hallucination Detector automatically detects hallucinated sources and poorly supported claims in essays.

claims.claim_text: The citation checker identifies hallucinated references instantly, helping educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification.
claims.evidence_span: Our citation checker identifies these hallucinated references instantly, helping educators maintain academic integrity without spending time on manual verification.

claims.claim_text: In the field of artificial intelligence, an artificial hallucination is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.
claims.evidence_span: In the field of artificial intelligence (AI), a hallucination or artificial hallucination (also called bullshitting,[1] confabulation,[3] delusion,[4] or mirage[5]) is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact.

claims.claim_text: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.
claims.evidence_span: Symbolic artificial intelligence models generally do not produce hallucinations, unlike large language models.

claims.claim_text: The survey aims to provide an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.
claims.evidence_span: The present survey aims to provide an extensive overview of current techniques employed to detect, verify, mitigate, or correct hallucinations in generative AI models.

claims.claim_text: Major detection and verification paradigms include retrieval-augmented generation, factuality evaluation metrics, automated fact-checking, natural language inference, knowledge-grounded reasoning, multi-model verification, and self-reflection-based approaches.
claims.evidence_span: Subsequently, we examine major detection and verification paradigms, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), factuality evaluation metrics, automated fact-checking, natural language inference (NLI), knowledge-grounded reasoning, multi-model verification, and self-reflection-based approaches.

claims.claim_text: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.
claims.evidence_span: AI hallucinations are instances where an AI system produces outputs that sound plausible but are factually wrong, irrelevant or entirely fabricated.

claims.claim_text: Engineers view hallucinations as an active research problem and a key barrier to reliable deployment, especially in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, legal and regulatory work.
claims.evidence_span: Engineers view hallucinations as an active research problem and a key barrier to reliable deployment, especially in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, finance, legal and regulatory work.

claims.claim_text: An AI hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.
claims.evidence_span: An AI hallucination is when a language model produces content that sounds authoritative and well-reasoned but is factually wrong or entirely made up.

claims.claim_text: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.
claims.evidence_span: Stanford research found that even specialized legal AI tools hallucinate between 17% and 34% of the time.
